causes.name: Battery fully drained
fixes: Plug it into a known-good charger and wall outlet (not a PC USB port).
Leave it charging 30 minutes before trying to power on - a deeply drained battery shows nothing at first.

causes.name: Device is on but frozen with screen off
fixes: Force restart. iPhone: Vol Up, Vol Down, then hold Side until the logo. Android: hold Power + Vol Down ~15 s. Laptop/console: hold power 15 s.

causes.name: Bad power cable, adapter or outlet
fixes: Try a different cable, adapter and wall socket.
Check the charger/adapter light (if it has one).
Desktop: confirm the switch on the back of the power supply is ON.

causes.name: Dirty or damaged charging port
fixes: Shine a light into the port; remove lint gently with a wooden toothpick or plastic pick. Never metal.

causes.name: Failed power supply (PSU)
fixes: Listen for fans / look for lights when you press power.
Test with a PSU tester or swap in a known-good PSU.

causes.name: Dead battery or failed board component
fixes: If nothing above works, get a repair quote - battery replacement is cheap; board repair may not be worth it on older devices.

causes.name: Lint in the charging port
fixes: Power off, then gently clear the port with a wooden toothpick.
Compressed air in short bursts, held upright.

causes.name: Faulty cable or adapter
fixes: Swap cable and adapter one at a time to find the bad part.
Use the manufacturer's charger or a certified one (USB-IF / MFi).

causes.name: Optimized / adaptive charging holding at 80%
fixes: iPhone: Settings > Battery > Charging. Android: Settings > Battery > Adaptive/Protect battery. macOS: Battery > Optimized charging.
This is normal behaviour, not a fault.

causes.name: Too hot or too cold
fixes: Let it reach room temperature; charging pauses outside ~0-35 C.
Remove thick cases while charging.

causes.name: Software charging glitch
fixes: Restart the device while plugged in.
Install pending system updates.

causes.name: Worn-out battery
fixes: Check battery health (iPhone: Settings > Battery > Battery Health; Windows: `powercfg /batteryreport`; macOS: System Settings > Battery).
Below ~80% capacity: replace the battery.

causes.name: App or process running in the background
fixes: Open the battery usage screen and find the top consumer.
Phone: Settings > Battery. Windows: Settings > System > Power & battery. macOS: Activity Monitor > Energy.
Force-quit or uninstall the offender; update it if it's an app bug.

causes.name: Screen brightness / always-on display
fixes: Turn on auto-brightness, shorten screen timeout, disable always-on display.

causes.name: Weak signal (phone searching for network)
fixes: In poor-signal areas switch to Wi-Fi calling or Airplane mode + Wi-Fi.

causes.name: Battery is old / degraded
fixes: Check battery health / cycle count (see 'Won't charge').
Lithium batteries last ~500-1000 cycles; replacement is the fix.

causes.name: Recent update re-indexing
fixes: After a major update, drain is normal for 1-2 days while it re-indexes.

causes.name: Lithium battery swelling (gas build-up)
fixes: STOP using and charging it now. Power it off.
Do not press on it, puncture it, or try to flatten it.
Keep it on a non-flammable surface away from anything that can burn.
Take it to a repair shop for battery replacement and dispose of the old battery at a battery recycling point - never in household trash.
causes.warning: FIRE RISK - a swollen battery can catch fire. Stop using it.

causes.name: Blocked vents / dust build-up
fixes: Use it on a hard flat surface, never a bed or lap blanket.
Blow out vents with compressed air (hold fans still while doing it).
Desktop/console: clean dust filters and heatsinks every 6-12 months.

causes.name: Heavy load (games, video, many apps)
fixes: Close apps you're not using; check Task Manager / Activity Monitor for anything using lots of CPU.

causes.name: Charging while doing heavy work, or in a thick case
fixes: Remove the case and avoid gaming while charging.

causes.name: Hot environment / direct sunlight
fixes: Move it out of the sun and away from heaters; let it cool before use.

causes.name: Dried-out thermal paste
fixes: On machines 3+ years old, re-pasting the CPU/GPU often drops temps 10-20 C. Doable at home on desktops; laptops/consoles - repair shop.

causes.name: Failing / swelling battery
fixes: If the case is bulging see 'Swollen battery' - stop using it.

causes.name: Storage almost full
fixes: Keep at least 10-15% of storage free.
Delete big unused apps, old downloads, duplicate photos/videos; move media to cloud or external storage.
Run `python diag_tool.py scan` on a computer to check disk space.

causes.name: Too many apps / tabs / startup programs
fixes: Restart the device - it clears memory and stuck processes.
Windows: Task Manager > Startup apps, disable what you don't need. macOS: System Settings > General > Login Items.
Close browser tabs; remove unneeded browser extensions.

causes.name: Overheating causing throttling
fixes: See 'Overheating' - hot chips slow themselves down on purpose.

causes.name: Malware or adware
fixes: Run a full scan (Windows Security / Malwarebytes).
Uninstall apps you don't recognise; reset browser settings.

causes.name: Outdated software
fixes: Install system and app updates.

causes.name: Old hard drive (HDD) or failing drive
fixes: Upgrading an HDD to an SSD is the single biggest speed-up for old PCs.
Check drive health: Windows `wmic diskdrive get status`, or CrystalDiskInfo; Linux `smartctl -a /dev/sda`.

causes.name: Not enough RAM for what you run
fixes: If memory is constantly >90% used, add RAM (desktops, some laptops).

causes.name: A buggy app or driver
fixes: Note what you were doing when it crashed - one app? Update or reinstall it.
Windows: update GPU/chipset drivers; check Event Viewer > Windows Logs > System.
macOS: check Console app > Crash Reports.

causes.name: Overheating
fixes: See 'Overheating'. Crashes under load + heat point here.

causes.name: Corrupt system update
fixes: Phone stuck in boot loop: boot to recovery and clear cache partition (Android) or update via computer (iPhone - Finder/Apple Devices app, choose 'Update' not 'Restore' to keep data).
Windows: Settings > System > Recovery > 'Fix problems using Windows Update'.

causes.name: Faulty RAM
fixes: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest86.
Reseat RAM sticks; test one stick at a time.

causes.name: Weak / failing power supply
fixes: Random restarts under load on a desktop often mean the PSU.

symptoms.title: Screen problems (black, flickering, lines, dead touch)

causes.name: Display asleep / brightness at zero
fixes: Press a key / tap / raise brightness. TV: check the input/source button.

causes.name: Loose or bad video cable / wrong input
fixes: Reseat HDMI/DisplayPort at both ends; try another cable and port.
TV/monitor: cycle through inputs with the Source button.

causes.name: Graphics driver problem
fixes: Windows: press Win+Ctrl+Shift+B to reset the graphics driver.
Update or reinstall the GPU driver.

causes.name: Screen protector / dirt causing bad touch
fixes: Clean the screen; remove a cracked or bubbled screen protector.

causes.name: Physical damage (crack, pressure, liquid)
fixes: Lines, colour blotches or black spots after a drop = panel damage. Screen replacement needed - get a quote before deciding.

causes.name: Loose display cable inside
fixes: Flicker that changes when you move a laptop lid points to the hinge cable - repair shop job.

causes.name: Router / modem needs a restart
fixes: Unplug the router AND modem for 30 seconds, plug the modem in first, wait for it to settle, then the router.

causes.name: Device network glitch
fixes: Toggle Wi-Fi/Bluetooth off and on; toggle Airplane mode.
'Forget' the network or Bluetooth device and reconnect.
Restart the device.

causes.name: Internet provider outage
fixes: Check from another device. If nothing works, check the provider's outage page / app using mobile data.

causes.name: Too far from router / interference
fixes: Move closer; use the 2.4 GHz band for range, 5 GHz for speed.
Consider a mesh system for big or multi-floor homes.

causes.name: Network settings corrupted
fixes: iPhone: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset > Reset Network Settings. Android: Settings > System > Reset options > Reset Wi-Fi & Bluetooth. Windows: Settings > Network > Advanced > Network reset.
This forgets saved Wi-Fi passwords.

causes.name: Router firmware out of date / overheating
fixes: Log into the router admin page and update firmware; keep it ventilated.

causes.name: Bluetooth device still paired to something else
fixes: Turn off Bluetooth on the other phone/PC, or put the device into pairing mode (usually hold the button until the light flashes).

symptoms.title: No sound / bad audio / mic not working

causes.name: Muted or wrong output device selected
fixes: Check volume, mute switch (iPhone side switch), and Do Not Disturb.
Computer: pick the right output in the sound settings / tray icon.
Phone: make sure it isn't still connected to Bluetooth headphones/car.

causes.name: Dirt in speaker / mic / earbud mesh
fixes: Brush gently with a soft dry toothbrush; for earbuds, a dry cotton swab.

causes.name: App permission for microphone denied
fixes: Settings > Privacy > Microphone - allow the app.

causes.name: Audio driver problem
fixes: Windows: Device Manager > Sound > uninstall device, then restart.

causes.name: Earbuds out of sync / unbalanced
fixes: Check the left/right balance in accessibility settings.
Reset the earbuds (put in case, hold the case button until the light flashes) and re-pair.

causes.name: Blown / damaged speaker
fixes: Crackling at every volume after a drop or water = hardware repair.

causes.name: Liquid inside the device
fixes: Power it off immediately. Do NOT charge it or plug it in.
Remove case, SIM tray, removable battery and accessories.
Wipe it dry, shake out gently with ports facing down.
Let it air-dry in a dry, ventilated place for 24-48 h (rice does NOT help and adds dust).
Sugary or salty liquid: get it to a repair shop soon - residue corrodes boards even after drying.
Laptop spill: turn it upside down in a tent shape immediately.
causes.warning: Do not charge or power on a wet device - it can short circuit.

causes.name: Photos, videos and messages filling storage
fixes: Back up photos to cloud/computer, then delete local copies.
Delete old message threads with big attachments.
iPhone: Settings > General > iPhone Storage. Android: Settings > Storage.

causes.name: Large apps / caches / downloads
fixes: Uninstall unused apps; clear app caches; empty Downloads and Trash.
Windows: Settings > System > Storage > Storage Sense.

symptoms.title: Buttons, keys or ports not working

causes.name: Dirt / debris under keys or in ports
fixes: Compressed air at an angle; clean ports with a plastic pick.

causes.name: Software / driver glitch
fixes: Restart; reconnect the accessory; update drivers/firmware.
Controller: re-pair and update controller firmware.

causes.name: Controller stick drift (worn sensor)
fixes: Recalibrate in the console's settings.
Persistent drift = stick module replacement (cheap part, fiddly job) or warranty claim.

causes.name: Physical wear or damage
fixes: Use accessibility shortcuts (on-screen keyboard / AssistiveTouch) until repaired.

causes.name: Printer offline / wrong printer selected
fixes: Turn the printer off and on; make sure it's on the same Wi-Fi.
Windows: Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers - set the right default, remove duplicate copies.
Restart the print spooler (Windows: services.msc > Print Spooler > Restart).

causes.name: Paper jam / scrap of paper inside
fixes: Power off, open all doors, pull paper out in the direction it travels.

causes.name: Clogged print head / low ink or toner
fixes: Run the print-head cleaning utility from the printer menu.
Replace low cartridges; shake laser toner gently.
